points.title: 早年求学
points.description: 伽利略1564年出生于意大利比萨，家庭为没落贵族。父亲文森佐·伽利莱是音乐理论家，对伽利略早期科学思维有重要影响。伽利略在比萨的修道院学校接受早期教育，后进入比萨大学学习医学，但很快转向对数学和物理学的兴趣。在此期间，他通过观察教堂吊灯的摆动，发现了摆的等时性原理，这一发现后来应用于计时器。比萨时期奠定了伽利略对实验科学的初步认识，尽管他尚未完全摆脱传统学术的束缚。
points.descriptionEn: Galileo was born in Pisa in 1564 to a family of fallen nobility. His father, Vincenzo Galilei, was a music theorist who significantly influenced Galileo's early scientific thinking. Galileo received his early education in a monastery school in Pisa and later enrolled at the University of Pisa to study medicine, but quickly shifted his interest to mathematics and physics. During this period, he observed the swinging of a chandelier in the cathedral and discovered the isochronism of the pendulum, a discovery later applied to timekeeping devices. The Pisa period laid the foundation for Galileo's understanding of experimental science, although he had not yet completely freed himself from the constraints of traditional academia.

points.title: 执教与实验
points.description: 1589年，伽利略回到比萨大学担任数学教授。在此期间，他进行了著名的落体实验，虽然可能并非从比萨斜塔上同时释放不同重量的球体，但确实通过斜面实验验证了物体下落速度与质量无关的原理。伽利略还发表了关于固体重心的论文，展示了他在力学方面的早期才能。然而，他的实验方法与亚里士多德学派的传统观点相冲突，导致与同事关系紧张。比萨时期的实验精神为伽利略后来的科学方法奠定了基础，但也预示了他与传统学术界的持续冲突。
points.descriptionEn: In 1589, Galileo returned to the University of Pisa as a professor of mathematics. During this period, he conducted his famous falling body experiments, though he likely did not simultaneously release balls of different weights from the Leaning Tower of Pisa. He did, however, verify through inclined plane experiments that the speed of falling objects is independent of their mass. Galileo also published a treatise on the center of gravity of solids, demonstrating his early talent in mechanics. However, his experimental methods conflicted with the traditional views of the Aristotelian school, leading to strained relationships with colleagues. The experimental spirit of his Pisa period laid the foundation for Galileo's later scientific methods but also foreshadowed his ongoing conflicts with the traditional academic world.

points.title: 黄金时期
points.description: 1592年，伽利略前往威尼斯共和国的帕多瓦大学任教，这是他一生中最富创造力的时期。在帕多瓦的18年间，他改进了望远镜并将其用于天文观测，发现了木星的四颗最大卫星（后被称为伽利略卫星）、月球表面的山脉和陨石坑、金星的相位变化以及太阳黑子。这些发现有力支持了哥白尼的日心说。伽利略还研究了力学，提出了惯性原理，并改进了军事罗盘和温度计。帕多瓦时期伽利略享有学术自由，与威尼斯共和国的宽松环境密不可分，这使他能够进行不受教会直接干预的研究工作。
points.descriptionEn: In 1592, Galileo moved to teach at the University of Padua in the Venetian Republic, which became the most creative period of his life. During his 18 years in Padua, he improved the telescope and used it for astronomical observations, discovering Jupiter's four largest moons (later called the Galilean moons), mountains and craters on the lunar surface, the phases of Venus, and sunspots. These discoveries provided strong support for Copernicus's heliocentric theory. Galileo also studied mechanics, proposing the principle of inertia, and improved the military compass and thermometer. The academic freedom Galileo enjoyed in Padua was closely linked to the宽松 environment of the Venetian Republic, allowing him to conduct research without direct interference from the Church.

points.title: 宫廷生活与冲突
points.description: 1610年，伽利略接受托斯卡纳大公科西莫二世的邀请，回到佛罗伦萨担任宫廷数学家和哲学家，结束了他在帕多瓦的教学生涯。这一时期，伽利略继续天文研究，并于1613年公开发表支持哥白尼日心说的观点。随着他与教会的矛盾加剧，1616年，宗教法庭警告伽利略不得坚持或辩护日心说。然而，1632年，伽利略出版了《关于两大世界体系的对话》，以对话形式支持日心说，激怒了教会。1633年，他被罗马宗教法庭审判，被迫放弃日心说并被软禁。佛罗伦萨时期见证了伽利略科学成就的顶峰，但也因与教会的冲突导致他晚年的悲剧。
points.descriptionEn: In 1610, Galileo accepted an invitation from Cosimo II de' Medici, Grand Duke of Tuscany, to return to Florence as court mathematician and philosopher, ending his teaching career in Padua. During this period, Galileo continued his astronomical research and publicly expressed support for the Copernican heliocentric theory in 1613. As his conflict with the Church intensified, the Inquisition warned Galileo in 1616 not to hold or defend the heliocentric theory. However, in 1632, Galileo published 'Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems,' which supported heliocentrism in dialogue form, angering the Church. In 1633, he was tried by the Roman Inquisition, forced to recant his support for heliocentrism, and placed under house arrest. The Florence period witnessed the peak of Galileo's scientific achievements but also led to the tragedy of his later years due to his conflict with the Church.

points.title: 晚年研究
points.description: 1633年被软禁后，伽利略被允许居住在佛罗伦萨附近的阿切特里，但受到严格监视。尽管如此，他在晚年仍继续科学研究，完成了《关于两种新科学的对话》，系统总结了他在力学和运动学方面的研究成果，包括惯性定律、加速度概念和抛物线运动理论。这部著作在他去世后出版，成为现代物理学的奠基之作之一。在阿切特里的最后岁月里，伽利略双目失明，但仍坚持科学研究，直到1642年去世。伽利略的晚年虽然充满限制，但他对科学的贡献和影响并未因此减少，反而通过他的著作继续影响着后世科学的发展。
points.descriptionEn: After being placed under house arrest in 1633, Galileo was allowed to live in Arcetri, near Florence, but under strict surveillance. Despite these restrictions, he continued his scientific research in his later years, completing 'Discourses and Mathematical Demonstrations Relating to Two New Sciences,' which systematically summarized his research in mechanics and kinematics, including the law of inertia, the concept of acceleration, and the theory of parabolic motion. This work was published after his death and became one of the foundational texts of modern physics. In his final years in Arcetri, Galileo became blind but persisted in his scientific work until his death in 1642. Although his later years were filled with limitations, Galileo's contributions to science and their impact did not diminish; instead, they continued to influence the development of science through his writings.

supporter.zh: 伽利略被誉为现代科学之父，他的实验方法和科学思维彻底改变了人类对自然界的认识。他通过望远镜观测证实了哥白尼的日心说，挑战了教会权威，为科学独立奠定了基础。伽利略的惯性定律和运动学研究为牛顿力学铺平了道路，他的科学方法论强调实验验证和数学分析，成为现代科学的基石。伽利略的精神遗产在于他坚持真理、勇于质疑权威的勇气，以及将实验与理论相结合的科学方法，这些至今仍是科学研究的核心原则。
supporter.en: Galileo is hailed as the father of modern science, whose experimental methods and scientific thinking revolutionized humanity's understanding of the natural world. His telescopic observations confirmed Copernicus's heliocentric theory, challenging church authority and laying the foundation for scientific independence. Galileo's laws of inertia and motion studies paved the way for Newtonian mechanics, and his scientific methodology emphasizing experimental verification and mathematical analysis became the cornerstone of modern science. Galileo's legacy lies in his courage to uphold truth and question authority, as well as his scientific method combining experiment with theory—principles that remain central to scientific research today.

critic.zh: 批评者指出伽利略的科学方法存在局限性，他的实验往往不够精确，有时过度依赖数学模型而忽视实际观测的复杂性。伽利略在对待日心说上的态度也被质疑，他可能过早地将尚未完全证实的理论视为真理。此外，伽利略与教会的冲突部分源于他个人性格的傲慢和缺乏外交手腕。他的《关于两大世界体系的对话》采用讽刺手法攻击亚里士多德学派，而非纯粹的科学论证，这种做法被批评为不够客观。这些批评反映了伽利略作为历史人物的复杂性和局限性，提醒我们即使是科学先驱也难免受到时代和个人因素的制约。
critic.en: Critics point out limitations in Galileo's scientific methods, noting that his experiments were often not precise enough and sometimes relied excessively on mathematical models while overlooking the complexity of actual observations. Galileo's attitude toward the heliocentric theory has also been questioned, as he may have prematurely accepted an unproven theory as truth. Additionally, his conflict with the church was partly due to his personal arrogance and lack of diplomatic skill. His 'Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems' used satire to attack Aristotelian scholars rather than purely scientific arguments, an approach criticized as lacking objectivity. These criticisms reflect the complexity and limitations of Galileo as a historical figure, reminding us that even scientific pioneers are inevitably constrained by the times and personal factors.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，伽利略被符号化为科学与宗教冲突的象征人物，代表着人类理性与权威的对抗。他的'但是，地球确实在运动'的临终遗言（尽管可能是后人杜撰）成为科学不屈精神的象征。伽利略的审判常被描绘为科学与宗教的永恒冲突，但历史研究表明这一关系更为复杂。现代科学史学者更倾向于将伽利略视为科学方法发展的关键人物，而非简单的反叛者。他的望远镜观测和力学研究确实推动了科学革命，但他的工作也建立在哥白尼、开普勒等前人的基础上。伽利略的形象在流行文化中不断被重塑，从受迫害的天才到科学方法的先驱，反映了不同时代对科学与社会关系的理解变化。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Galileo has been symbolized as a figure representing the conflict between science and religion, embodying the struggle between human reason and authority. His alleged last words, 'And yet it moves,' though possibly apocryphal, have become a symbol of scientific resilience. Galileo's trial is often portrayed as an eternal conflict between science and religion, but historical research indicates this relationship was more complex. Modern historians of science tend to view Galileo as a pivotal figure in the development of scientific methods rather than simply a rebel. His telescopic observations and mechanics research did advance the Scientific Revolution, but his work also built upon that of predecessors like Copernicus and Kepler. Galileo's image has been continuously reshaped in popular culture, from persecuted genius to pioneer of scientific methods, reflecting changing understandings of the relationship between science and society across different eras.

self.zh: 数学是上帝用来描述宇宙的语言。
self.en: Mathematics is the language with which God has written the universe.

others.zh: 伽利略是现代科学之父，他教会了我们如何思考，而不是思考什么。
others.en: Galileo is the father of modern science; he taught us how to think, not what to think.
